findings.description: The emitted extract stops at ## Raw Content, verified from the file on disk rather than from the migrator's documentation.
findings.evidence:
<scratch>/i59pVI65GO.extract.md ends at line 28 with the last memory-candidate bullet, then a single blank line; its final section heading is "## Action Items / Memory Candidates". The string "Raw Content" does not appear in either emitted extract.

Source note tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/evals/tier2-summary-entities/notes/2025-09-08-kestrel-cutover-planning-i59pVI65GO.md:44-48 carries "## Raw Content" at :44 and three lines of transcript at :46-48, none of which reach the extract.

findings.description: The planted contrast holds in both directions: the below-fence name and fact are absent from the extract and present in the note, while the proposable entities appear verbatim in the extract.
findings.evidence:
String-by-string, note vs. emitted extract (grep -Fc):
  "Tomas Krohl"    note:1  extract:0
  "November 14th"  note:1  extract:0
  "four hours"     note:1  extract:0
  "Tomasz Krol"    note:3  extract:2
  "Elena Vasquez"  note:3  extract:2

The plants sit below the fence: note :46 "Tomas Krohl said the staging rebuild finished in four hours this run...", :47 "...the team locked the cutover for November 14th." "Tomas Krohl" is a mishearing of "Tomasz Krol", who is real and sourced (extract :5, :9).

Exercised the contrast against the migrator itself, on a copy of the fixture staged outside the repo:
  entities: ['Tomas Krohl'] -> "tier2-entity-unsourced: \"Tomas Krohl\" does not appear in this note's Tier 2 extract; left alone"
  entities: ['Elena Vasquez', 'Tomasz Krol'] -> no tier2 finding; the note migrates.
So the wrong proposal is machine-rejected and the right one is not, which is the contrast the fixture exists to create. The November 14th cutover date gives the summary half its unsourced fact: a plausible summary asserting it cites something the reviewed layer never said.

findings.description: Both extracts carry enough substance to make a one-line summary possible, so the summary rows are scoreable in both directions.
findings.evidence:
<scratch>/i59pVI65GO.extract.md holds six populated sections across 28 lines: two attributed quotes, a named tension (Elena's Tuesday window against Tomasz's Thursday-to-Sunday rebuild buffer), stated and unstated assumptions, two open questions, and three action/candidate bullets. A sourced one-liner is straightforward, e.g. "Elena and Tomasz disagree on the cutover window because the index rebuild needs a multi-day buffer" — every element traceable to extract :9.

<scratch>/bARPVZN8s6.extract.md is thinner but not filler: a quote, a tension with a named unresolved deadline, two assumptions, an open question, and an action item. Also summarizable in one line.

findings.evidence:

v1 files: 4

Noting what this does not say: v2 files is 0, so the token checks at lint-scope.sh:421-448 read none of these notes' tokens. Part (b) below is the check that actually covers them.

findings.description: Well-formedness part (b): the tokens surviving the linter's own four-step extraction are all registered shapes with legal enumerated values.
findings.evidence:
Replicated the four steps by hand over all four notes/records (no CLAUDE.md or README.md in the fixture, so :418-419's exclusion is vacuous here): extract_body per :208-216, then sed 's/\[\[[^]]*\]\]//g' per :218-222, then grep -oE '\[[a-z][a-z0-9 -]*(:|\])' | sort -u.

Surviving tokens, whole fixture:
  2025-09-08-...-i59pVI65GO.md: [memory candidate:
  2025-09-22-...-bARPVZN8s6.md: (none)
  _memory/context/index-rebuild-duration-_YEL9dotcZ.md: (none)
  _memory/decisions/cutover-rebuild-buffer-8taS8NdrXK.md: (none)

Full bracketed strings in the extracted bodies, for the enum check:
  i59: '[ ]' (checkbox, not token-shaped — the regex requires [a-z] first), '[memory candidate: project]', '[memory candidate: client]'
  bARPVZN8s6: '[ ]'

'[memory candidate:' is row 1/2 of the ten-row grammar table at references/machine-contracts.md:69-70, and both scope values are inside the registered set (lint-scope.sh:234 admits project|client|update existing ). No token outside the table, no enumerated value outside its row.

On the boundary the task flags: the below-fence transcript at note :46-48 contains no brackets at all, so there was nothing down there to misreport. extract_body stops at :44 regardless.
